segments.he: גת כו' או כו'. לשון הטור ומ"ש ונתן כו' רש"י שם ד"ה גת וכ"כ בת"ה ועש"ך שכתב כלומר לאחר זפיתה כו' [וכ"כ דו"פ] והוא מדברי מרדכי שם שכתב גת שזפתה משום שנתן יין בשעת זפיתה ולרב זביד דאמר לעיל פ"ב דנעשה כזורק כו' מ"מ אסור דשמא נתן בה יין אחר זפיתה אבל דברי רש"י ות"ה וטור שכתבו בשעת זפיתה הוא ע"פ סה"ת סוף סי' ק"ס שכתב בשם ר"ת דר"ז ל"ק אלא בנודות דזוהמא דעור מפיג טעם היין כו':
segments.en: A winepress, etc. or, etc. The Tur's wording; and what is written "and he put," etc. ; Rashi there on "winepress"; and likewise in Torah HaBayit; and Shach wrote: meaning after pitching it, etc. [and likewise in Darkei Moshe]; and he speaks of Mordechai's words there who wrote: a winepress that he pitched ; because he put wine at the time of pitching; and for Rav Zevid who said above chapter 2 "it is like throwing," etc. ; nevertheless forbidden, lest he put wine in it after pitching; but the words of Rashi and Torah HaBayit and Tur who wrote "at the time of pitching" are according to Sefat Emet end of siman 160 who wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Tam that R. Zeira did not challenge except regarding skins whose filth of hide spoils the taste of wine, etc.

segments.he: או שזפתה כו'. ת"ה וכמש"ש ס' ב' ההוא עובד כוכבים דאשתכח כו' ועמ"ש למטה:
segments.en: Or if he pitched it, etc. Torat HaBayit, as stated there on 60b concerning the non-Jew who was found, etc. See what I write below.

segments.he: טופח. ע"מ להטפיח כמש"ש. שם בת"ה:
segments.en: Moist. Moist enough to moisten another surface, as stated there. This is stated in Torat HaBayit.

segments.he: בזפותה. רש"י שם ד"ה אבל דרך בה עובד כוכבים כו' דס"ל דל"פ הני לישני דאל"כ יהיו הלשונות שני היפוכים ועתוס' די"ט י"ג א' ד"ה א"ד כו' וכ"כ הרא"ש והרשב"א ואע"ג דרשב"א ל"ג תרי לישני מ"מ מוכח מברייתא להדיא דבזפותה מיירי כמש"ש ברייתא דדרך בה ואפ"ה סגי בניגוב בשאינן מזופתין אלא דלרש"י ותוס' דגרסי לתרוייהו צ"ל כמש"ש בתוס' ד"ה הגת כו' וי"ל דמתני' כו':
segments.en: When pitching it. Rashi there on "but the way of a gentile in it," etc. ; for he holds these two versions are not otherwise two opposite versions; and Tosafot Avodah Zarahh 13a on "I say," etc.; and likewise the Rosh and Rashba; and even though Rashba does not accept two versions, nevertheless it is proven from the braita explicitly that it deals with pitching it, as stated regarding the braita "the way in it"; and nevertheless wiping-dry suffices when they are not pitched ; but for Rashi and Tosafot who have both versions, it must be as stated in Tosafot on "the winepress," etc.; and one can say the mishnah, etc.

segments.he: אלא יקלוף כו'. רש"י שם בד"ה לא סגי כו' והרא"ש וש"פ וכמש"ש כי ההוא כו' לסיועיה לרבא ופי' בת"ה שלקח גת חדש מהעובד כוכבים ומתוך שראה רב שחלק כ"כ סבור שלא דרך בה וכדחזי בה פילי אמר ודאי דרך בה וכן תניא בתוספתא של עץ ושל אבן צריך לנגב ואם היו זפותין צריך לקלף כו' ובשדרך בה כמ"ש בגמ' שם. ת"ה:
segments.en: Rather, he must peel off, etc. Rashi there, s.v. lo sagi, etc., the Rosh, and the other authorities, as follows from the incident cited there in support of Rava. Torat HaBayit explains that Rav bought a new winepress from a non-Jew. Because he saw that it was very smooth, he assumed that wine had not been pressed in it. When he saw cracks in it, he said that wine had certainly been pressed in it. The Tosefta likewise teaches that a wooden or stone press requires wiping, and if it is pitched the pitch must be peeled off, etc., when wine was pressed in it, as stated in the Gemara there. Torat HaBayit.

segments.he: או עירוי כו'. הרא"ש והרשב"א. וכמש"ש ל"ג א' ל"ש נודות ל"ש כו' ובזפותים מיירי דאל"כ א"צ בנודות כ"א שכשוך כמש"ש וכמש"ל סי' קל"ה ס"א:
segments.en: Or iruy, etc. The Rosh and Rashba; and as stated "one version ; skins, one version," etc.; and it deals with pitched ones, for otherwise skins would not need [peeling] but only rubbing, as stated; and as stated above siman 135 seif 1.

segments.he: (ליקוט) או עירוי בלא קליפה. דלעירוי א"צ לעולם קליפה ממ"ש ל"ג א' ת"ר קנקנים כו' מזופפים אסורים כו' ישראל נותן לתוכו מים ר"ל עירוי ג"י כמ"ש רש"י ותוס' שם אלמא מהני במזופף. ר"נ ספ"ה (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) Or iruy without peeling ; for iruy never requires peeling, from what is stated "one version: the Tanna taught jars," etc. "pitched ; forbidden," etc. "Israel puts water into it" ; meaning iruy three days, as Rashi and Tosafot wrote there ; thus it helps in pitched [vessels]. Ran end of perek 5 (end).

segments.he: או יישנה יב"ח. כמש"ש ע"ה א' ב' דיישון מהני לכל וכמש"ל ס"ס קל"ה:
segments.en: Or he ages it twelve months. As stated Avodah Zarahh 1:2 ; aging helps for everything; and as stated above siman 135.

segments.he: ונתן כו'. כנ"ל:
segments.en: And he placed, etc. As above.

segments.he: אפילו לא כו'. דמתני' בהכי מיירי כנ"ל:
segments.en: Even if he did not, etc. The mishnah addresses precisely such a case, as above.

segments.he: או שזפתה ודרך כו'. בברייתא שם ואוקמוה בדרך בה ותניא בתוספתא דיקלוף כנ"ל:
segments.en: Or if he pitched it and pressed, etc. This is taught in the baraita there, which the Gemara establishes as referring to a case where wine was pressed in it. The Tosefta teaches that the pitch must be peeled off, as above.

segments.he: או שזפתה ישראל כו'. עתוס' שם ד"ה הגת כו' וי"ל כו' וא"ת א"כ כו' ד"ל בכה"ג דהא מתני' בלא דרך בה:
segments.en: Or Israel pitched it, etc. See Tosafot there on "the winepress," etc.; and one can say, etc.; and you will not find, etc. ; he speaks in such a case, for the mishnah [deals] without "the way in it."

segments.he: או עירוי כו'. כנ"ל:
segments.en: Or soaking, etc. As above.

segments.he: ואם יש כו'. כמש"ש ע"ה א' דבקטרי לא מהני ניגוב וכ' בת"ה דדוקא ניגוב אבל עירוי מהני וכמש"ל בס"ט והני כי קטרי דמי. ב"י ודו"פ ועבת"ה:
segments.en: And if there are, etc. As stated on 75a, wiping is ineffective where there are knots. Torat HaBayit writes that this applies only to wiping, but soaking is effective, as stated above in seif 9; these are comparable to knots. Beit Yosef, Derishah and Perishah; see Torat HaBayit.

segments.he: או הגעלה. שם נעוה ארתחו וערא"ש סל"א ושל חרס כו' ולהכי אמר כו' וכ"ש כאן:
segments.en: Or hag'alah. There Na'aveh Artacho; and the Rosh siman 31; and regarding earthenware, etc.; and therefore he said, etc.; and all the more so here.

segments.he: ונתן כו'. כנ"ל:
segments.en: And he placed, etc. As above.

segments.he: אפי' לא כו'. כאוקימתא דרבא הנ"ל:
segments.en: Even if he did not, etc. In accordance with Rava's aforementioned explanation.

segments.he: או שזפתה כו'. כמ"ש בתוס' הנ"ל ד"ה הגת כו' וכנ"ל:
segments.en: Or he pitched it, etc. As stated in the aforementioned Tosafot on "the winepress," etc.; and as above.

segments.he: אלא במילוי כו'. וכמ"ש בקנקנים זפותים כנ"ל:
segments.en: Rather, through filling, etc. As stated regarding pitched jars, above.

segments.he: ואם זפתה כו' או כו'. דלהכי אמר נעוה ארתחו ולא קאמר בעירוי אבל הג"א פ"ב סכ"ב ד"ה וכן כ' דלכל כלי מהני עירוי וכ"ד כל הפוסקים:
segments.en: And if he pitched it, etc. or, etc. ; therefore Na'aveh Artacho said and did not speak of iruy; but Hagahot Ashiri chapter 2 seif 22 wrote that for every vessel iruy helps; and so say all poskim.

segments.he: (ליקוט) צריכה קליפה ומילוי ועירוי. כ"כ הרא"ש אבל כל הפוסקים חולקים על זה ושגגה היא דהא אמרינן שם ומורה ר' בקנקנים כו' אלמא קנקנים חמורים מגת שדרך בה דהא ברייתא בדרך ומסתמא קנקנים כעין גת שאינה זפותה [וכ"כ רש"י ור"נ שם] מדקאמר ומה הפרש כו' ואמרינן ל"ג א' קנקנים כו' מזופפין כו' ישראל נותן לתוכו מים וכ"ש לגת זפותה שדרך וכ"ד כל הפוסקים וראייתו ממ"ש נעוה ארתחו דחויה דהיתר הגעלה בכ"ח השמיענו (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) It requires peeling, filling, and iruy ; likewise the Rosh; but all poskim disagree on this and it is an error, for we say there "and R. teaches regarding jars," etc. ; thus jars are more stringent than a winepress that is trodden in, for the braita [deals with] trodden in; and presumably jars are like a winepress that is not pitched [and likewise Rashi and Ran there] from what it says "and what is the difference," etc.; and we say "one version: jars," etc. "pitched," etc. "Israel puts water into it" ; and all the more so for a pitched winepress that is trodden in; and so say all poskim; and his proof from what Na'aveh Artacho wrote is rejected ; for he informed us of the heter of hag'alah in earthenware (end).

segments.he: או יישנן כו'. כנ"ל:
segments.en: Or he ages them, etc. As above.

segments.he: (ליקוט) או יישנן יב"ח. דמהני אפי' לקנקנים כמש"ש ל"ד וע"כ איירי בזפותים מדקאמר ג"כ נודות והן מותרין בלא זפיתה כמש"ש (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) Or he ages them twelve months ; for it helps even for jars, as stated "one version"; and perforce it deals with pitched ones, from what it says "also skins" and they are permitted without pitching, as stated (end).

segments.he: או להסיקה כו'. דהוא כמו הגעלה כמ"ש בתוס' ל"ג ב' ד"ה קינסא והג"א וש"פ וכמש"ל סי' קל"ה סי"ד:
segments.en: Or heat it, etc. This is equivalent to hagalah, as Tosafot 33b, s.v. kinnesa, Hagahot Ashri, and the other authorities write, and as stated above, siman 135, seif 14.

segments.he: וכ"ז בזפותה. דבזפותה אין חילוק בין תחלת תשמישן ע"י עובד כוכבים או ע"י ישראל בין בכלי עץ ואבן בין בכ"ח טור ועתוס' שם ד"ה הגת כו' וי"ל דבמזופפין כו':
segments.en: All this applies when it is pitched. With a pitched vessel there is no distinction whether its initial use was by a non-Jew or by a Jew, whether it is wood or stone, or whether it is earthenware. Tur. See Tosafot there, s.v. hageit, etc.: ‘one may say that with pitched vessels,’ etc.

segments.he: אבל כו' שאם כו'. שם בברייתא ת"ר הגת כו' של עץ כו' ואם כו' ובתוס' הנ"ל כשאינן כו' וי"ל דמתני' כו' ובדרך בה מיירי כמ"ש בהג"ה אם דרך בה וכמש"ש ברייתא כו' וכמ"ש בתוס' שם ולקמן מוקמינן כו' וי"ל כו' לפי שהרבה פעמים דרך כו':
segments.en: But, etc. "if," etc. There in the braita the Tanna taught: "a winepress," etc. "of wood," etc. "and if," etc.; and in the aforementioned Tosafot "when they are not," etc.; and one can say the mishnah, etc.; and it deals with trodden in, as stated in the hagahah "if trodden in"; and as stated regarding the braita, etc.; and as stated in Tosafot there; and below we establish, etc.; and one can say, etc. ; because many times he trod, etc.

segments.he: (ליקוט) שאם תחלת כו' ואם תחלת כו'. עתוס' ד"ה הגת כו' וי"ל דמתני' כו' וכ"כ הר"נ ויש כאן גי' אחרת לרש"י שהוא גורס לישנא קמא בגמרא כו' והקשו עליו בתוס' כו' ותי' דברייתא בתחלת תשמישו באיסור וכדקתני הגת כו' של עובדי כוכבים כו' אבל מתני' בגת של ישראל עסקינן ותחלת תשמישו בהיתר וכ' אבל לגי' הרי"ף אפילו תחלת תשמישו בהיתר צריכה ניגוב וכ' שנ"ל גי' הרי"ף עיקר (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) "That if at the beginning," etc. "and if at the beginning," etc. ; see Tosafot on "the winepress," etc.; and one can say the mishnah, etc.; and likewise Ran; and there is here another version of Rashi who has the first version in the Gemara, etc.; and they challenged him in Tosafot, etc.; and Tosafot explain the braita: at the beginning of its use in issur ; and as the mishnah teaches "a winepress," etc. "of idolaters," etc.; but the mishnah deals with a winepress of Israel whose beginning of use is in heter; and he wrote: but for the Rif's version, even if the beginning of its use is in heter it requires wiping-dry; and he wrote as we said the Rif's version is primary (end).

segments.he: ובשל חרס כו'. כחכמים בברייתא שם:
segments.en: And with earthenware, etc. In accordance with the Sages in the baraita there.

segments.he: אם דרך בה. כ"כ בטור ואם דרך באינה זפותה צריכה עירוי והוא תמוה דהא הרא"ש שם סל"א כתב דניגוב אינו מפליט בכלי חרס וכ"כ בת"ה ושל חרס אע"פ כו' ולפיכך לא סגי לה בניגוב ואפילו אם נגבה לאחר שקלפה אלא מילוי ועירוי כו' וכן הדין בשאינה זפותה שהחרס בולע הרבה וכבר כ' למעלה שאין הכלים המזופתין בולעין יותר מחמת זפתן ממה שהיו בלא זפת [וכ"כ הר"ן בפ"ב שם ומ"מ אם קלף זפתן מותרין כו' שאין הזפת בולע יותר כו' ע"ש] וכ"כ בסה"ת להדיא וערש"י שם ד"ה והא אנן תנן כו' אלמא כו' וכ"כ ברא"ש פ"ב סכ"א ואין חילוק בין היה בו זפת ונקלף ובין לא היה בו זפת מעולם כדמוכח לקמן בפ' בתרא כו' ע"ש וכ"כ בסה"ת ובתוס' שם וכ"מ שם דקאמר ומודה רבי כו' ומה הפרש כו' וע"כ בקנקנים שאינן זפותין דקאמר ומודה כו' ומה כו' ואם איתא גם לרבנן קשה מה הפרש כו'. והאי דרך בה צ"ל קודם ובשל חרס ואעץ ואבן כנ"ל וע"ל סי' קל"ה ס"ד דאפילו בשאר כ"ח תחלת תשמישן ע"י עובד כוכבים צריך עירוי:
segments.en: If trodden in. Likewise in the Tur; and if trodden in when it is not pitched it requires iruy ; and this is astonishing, for the Rosh there siman 31 wrote that wiping-dry does not expel from earthenware; and likewise in Torah HaBayit; and regarding earthenware even though, etc.; and therefore wiping-dry does not suffice for it, and even if he wiped after peeling ; only filling and iruy, etc.; and the same law applies when it is not pitched, for earthenware absorbs much; and he already wrote above that pitched vessels do not absorb more because of their pitch than they would without pitch [and likewise Ran in chapter 2 there; nevertheless if he peeled their pitch they are permitted, etc. ; see there]; and likewise in Sefat Emet explicitly; and the Rosh there on "but we learned," etc. ; thus, etc.; and likewise in the Rosh chapter 2 seif 1; and there is no distinction between there was pitch and it was peeled and between there was never pitch, as proven below in the last chapter, etc. ; see there; and likewise in Sefat Emet and in Tosafot there; and in many places there it says "and R. concedes," etc. "and what is the difference," etc.; and perforce in jars that are not pitched, where it says "and he concedes," etc. "and what," etc.; and if it were so, also for the Rabbis it would be difficult ; what is the difference, etc. And this "trodden in" must be beforehand; and in earthenware and wood and stone as above; and see siman 135 seif 4 that even in other earthenware vessels whose beginning of use is by a gentile, iruy is required.

segments.he: ואם תחלת כו'. הוא לישנא קמא דרבא וכמ"ש בתוס' הנ"ל וכ"כ בסה"ת ורשב"א וערא"ש סל"ג ועוד י"ל כו' ובתוס' ע"ב ב' ד"ה אם כו':
segments.en: And if its initial use, etc. This is Rava's first version, as stated in the aforementioned Tosafot. Sefer HaTerumah and Rashba likewise rule this way. See Rosh, seif 33: ‘one may further say,’ etc., and Tosafot 72b, s.v. im, etc.

segments.he: אם היא של עץ. דאין חילוק בינה לאבן רק במזופתין וערש"י במתני' שם ד"ה ושל עץ כו' וברא"ש פ"ב סכ"ב:
segments.en: If it is wooden. There is no distinction between wood and stone except where they are pitched. See Rashi on the mishnah there, s.v. veshel etz, etc., and Rosh, perek 2, seif 22.

segments.he: אבל כו'. בת"ה ומיהו אף חכמים לא הצריכו בשל חרס מילוי ועירוי אלא בתחלת תשמישה ביד עובד כוכבים כו' אבל בתחלת תשמישה ביד ישראל בניגוב סגי וז"ש המחץ כו' של עובדי כוכבים דאל"כ ל"ל דקתני של עובדי כוכבים וכ"ד הראב"ד ז"ל עכ"ל ומ"מ דוקא בשאין מזופתין דבמזופתין אין חילוק כנ"ל:
segments.en: But, etc. In Torah HaBayit; and nevertheless even the Sages did not require filling and iruy in earthenware except at the beginning of its use in a gentile's hand, etc.; but at the beginning of its use in a Jew's hand, wiping-dry suffices ; and this is what Machatz wrote, etc. "of idolaters" ; for otherwise why does it teach "of idolaters"; and so said Raavad z"l ; end; and nevertheless specifically when they are not pitched, for in pitched ones there is no distinction as above.

segments.he: (ליקוט) אבל כו' צריכה ניגוב. הוא דעת הראב"ד אבל הר"נ חולק שם וכתב מדקתני במתני' סתמא אסורה משמע אפילו תחלת תשמישו ע"י ישראל והא דקתני בברייתא של עבודת כוכבים לרבותא דאפ"ה מתיר רבי וכ"ז לגי' הרי"ף אבל לגי' תוס' שכ' ש"ע ע"כ מתני' בתחלת תשמיש ע"י ישראל וצע"ג (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) But, etc. requires wiping-dry ; this is Raavad's view; but Ran disagrees there and wrote: from what the mishnah teaches anonymously "forbidden," it implies even if the beginning of its use is by Israel; and that which the braita teaches "of idolatry" is to include that nevertheless R. permits; and all this is for the Rif's version; but for Tosafot's version who wrote Shulchan Aruch ; end ; the mishnah [deals with] at the beginning of use by Israel; and it requires study (end).

segments.he: (ליקוט) אבל אם היא של חרס צריכה ניגוב. צ"ע דהא מתני' בתחלת תשמישה ע"י ישראל כמ"ש תוס' וכנ"ל ואפילו באינה זפותה אסורה כמש"ש אע"פ שקלף כו' וה"ה באינה זפותה כנ"ל ואף שתי' תוס' וי"ל דמתני' י"ל בענין אחר לפי שעה או הרבה מ"מ מלשון הטור שמחלק בין תחלתה ע"י עובד כוכבים או ישראל משמע שמפרש תי' תוס' בכה"ג ואף שבת"ה כ' כן היינו לפי גי' דל"ג לישנא קמא וא"צ לתי' תוס' אבל לדידן קשה. וכמ"ש הרא"ש שאין ניגוב מועיל לכ"ח וכנ"ל ולא דמי לכסי שחילקו בפ"ב (ל"ג ב') בין תחלת תשמישן ביד ישראל כו' ששם אינן טרודין ביין בשפע כמו גת כמ"ש הר"נ שלכן אפי' ניגוב לא בעי אבל כאן בכ"ע בעירוי (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) But if it is earthenware it requires wiping-dry ; it requires study, for the mishnah [deals with] at the beginning of its use by Israel, as Tosafot wrote and as above; and even when it is not pitched it is forbidden, as stated "even though he peeled," etc.; and the same applies when it is not pitched as above; and even though Tosafot wrote "and one can say the mishnah," etc. ; for a temporary matter or many times; nevertheless from the Tur's language, who distinguishes between its beginning by a gentile or by Israel, it implies he explains Tosafot's answer in such a case; and even though in Torah HaBayit he wrote thus ; that was according to the version that does not have the first version, and Tosafot's answer is not needed; but for us it is difficult. And as the Rosh wrote that wiping-dry does not help for earthenware, as above; and it is not comparable to a cover that they distinguished in chapter 2 (one version 2) between the beginning of their use in a Jew's hand, etc. ; for there they are not constantly occupied with wine abundantly as in a winepress, as Ran wrote; therefore even wiping-dry is not required; but here in all cases iruy is required (end).

en_segments: A winepress, etc. or, etc. The Tur's wording; and what is written "and he put," etc. ; Rashi there on "winepress"; and likewise in Torah HaBayit; and Shach wrote: meaning after pitching it, etc. [and likewise in Darkei Moshe]; and he speaks of Mordechai's words there who wrote: a winepress that he pitched ; because he put wine at the time of pitching; and for Rav Zevid who said above chapter 2 "it is like throwing," etc. ; nevertheless forbidden, lest he put wine in it after pitching; but the words of Rashi and Torah HaBayit and Tur who wrote "at the time of pitching" are according to Sefat Emet end of siman 160 who wrote in the name of Rabbeinu Tam that R. Zeira did not challenge except regarding skins whose filth of hide spoils the taste of wine, etc.
Or if he pitched it, etc. Torat HaBayit, as stated there on 60b concerning the non-Jew who was found, etc. See what I write below.
Moist. Moist enough to moisten another surface, as stated there. This is stated in Torat HaBayit.

When pitching it. Rashi there on "but the way of a gentile in it," etc. ; for he holds these two versions are not otherwise two opposite versions; and Tosafot Avodah Zarahh 13a on "I say," etc.; and likewise the Rosh and Rashba; and even though Rashba does not accept two versions, nevertheless it is proven from the braita explicitly that it deals with pitching it, as stated regarding the braita "the way in it"; and nevertheless wiping-dry suffices when they are not pitched ; but for Rashi and Tosafot who have both versions, it must be as stated in Tosafot on "the winepress," etc.; and one can say the mishnah, etc.

Rather, he must peel off, etc. Rashi there, s.v. lo sagi, etc., the Rosh, and the other authorities, as follows from the incident cited there in support of Rava. Torat HaBayit explains that Rav bought a new winepress from a non-Jew. Because he saw that it was very smooth, he assumed that wine had not been pressed in it. When he saw cracks in it, he said that wine had certainly been pressed in it. The Tosefta likewise teaches that a wooden or stone press requires wiping, and if it is pitched the pitch must be peeled off, etc., when wine was pressed in it, as stated in the Gemara there. Torat HaBayit.

Or iruy, etc. The Rosh and Rashba; and as stated "one version ; skins, one version," etc.; and it deals with pitched ones, for otherwise skins would not need [peeling] but only rubbing, as stated; and as stated above siman 135 seif 1.

(Extract) Or iruy without peeling ; for iruy never requires peeling, from what is stated "one version: the Tanna taught jars," etc. "pitched ; forbidden," etc. "Israel puts water into it" ; meaning iruy three days, as Rashi and Tosafot wrote there ; thus it helps in pitched [vessels]. Ran end of perek 5 (end).
Or he ages it twelve months. As stated Avodah Zarahh 1:2 ; aging helps for everything; and as stated above siman 135.
And he placed, etc. As above.
Even if he did not, etc. The mishnah addresses precisely such a case, as above.

Or if he pitched it and pressed, etc. This is taught in the baraita there, which the Gemara establishes as referring to a case where wine was pressed in it. The Tosefta teaches that the pitch must be peeled off, as above.
Or Israel pitched it, etc. See Tosafot there on "the winepress," etc.; and one can say, etc.; and you will not find, etc. ; he speaks in such a case, for the mishnah [deals] without "the way in it."
Or soaking, etc. As above.

And if there are, etc. As stated on 75a, wiping is ineffective where there are knots. Torat HaBayit writes that this applies only to wiping, but soaking is effective, as stated above in seif 9; these are comparable to knots. Beit Yosef, Derishah and Perishah; see Torat HaBayit.
Or hag'alah. There Na'aveh Artacho; and the Rosh siman 31; and regarding earthenware, etc.; and therefore he said, etc.; and all the more so here.
And he placed, etc. As above.
Even if he did not, etc. In accordance with Rava's aforementioned explanation.
Or he pitched it, etc. As stated in the aforementioned Tosafot on "the winepress," etc.; and as above.
Rather, through filling, etc. As stated regarding pitched jars, above.
And if he pitched it, etc. or, etc. ; therefore Na'aveh Artacho said and did not speak of iruy; but Hagahot Ashiri chapter 2 seif 22 wrote that for every vessel iruy helps; and so say all poskim.

(Extract) It requires peeling, filling, and iruy ; likewise the Rosh; but all poskim disagree on this and it is an error, for we say there "and R. teaches regarding jars," etc. ; thus jars are more stringent than a winepress that is trodden in, for the braita [deals with] trodden in; and presumably jars are like a winepress that is not pitched [and likewise Rashi and Ran there] from what it says "and what is the difference," etc.; and we say "one version: jars," etc. "pitched," etc. "Israel puts water into it" ; and all the more so for a pitched winepress that is trodden in; and so say all poskim; and his proof from what Na'aveh Artacho wrote is rejected ; for he informed us of the heter of hag'alah in earthenware (end).
Or he ages them, etc. As above.

(Extract) Or he ages them twelve months ; for it helps even for jars, as stated "one version"; and perforce it deals with pitched ones, from what it says "also skins" and they are permitted without pitching, as stated (end).
Or heat it, etc. This is equivalent to hagalah, as Tosafot 33b, s.v. kinnesa, Hagahot Ashri, and the other authorities write, and as stated above, siman 135, seif 14.

All this applies when it is pitched. With a pitched vessel there is no distinction whether its initial use was by a non-Jew or by a Jew, whether it is wood or stone, or whether it is earthenware. Tur. See Tosafot there, s.v. hageit, etc.: ‘one may say that with pitched vessels,’ etc.

But, etc. "if," etc. There in the braita the Tanna taught: "a winepress," etc. "of wood," etc. "and if," etc.; and in the aforementioned Tosafot "when they are not," etc.; and one can say the mishnah, etc.; and it deals with trodden in, as stated in the hagahah "if trodden in"; and as stated regarding the braita, etc.; and as stated in Tosafot there; and below we establish, etc.; and one can say, etc. ; because many times he trod, etc.

(Extract) "That if at the beginning," etc. "and if at the beginning," etc. ; see Tosafot on "the winepress," etc.; and one can say the mishnah, etc.; and likewise Ran; and there is here another version of Rashi who has the first version in the Gemara, etc.; and they challenged him in Tosafot, etc.; and Tosafot explain the braita: at the beginning of its use in issur ; and as the mishnah teaches "a winepress," etc. "of idolaters," etc.; but the mishnah deals with a winepress of Israel whose beginning of use is in heter; and he wrote: but for the Rif's version, even if the beginning of its use is in heter it requires wiping-dry; and he wrote as we said the Rif's version is primary (end).
And with earthenware, etc. In accordance with the Sages in the baraita there.

If trodden in. Likewise in the Tur; and if trodden in when it is not pitched it requires iruy ; and this is astonishing, for the Rosh there siman 31 wrote that wiping-dry does not expel from earthenware; and likewise in Torah HaBayit; and regarding earthenware even though, etc.; and therefore wiping-dry does not suffice for it, and even if he wiped after peeling ; only filling and iruy, etc.; and the same law applies when it is not pitched, for earthenware absorbs much; and he already wrote above that pitched vessels do not absorb more because of their pitch than they would without pitch [and likewise Ran in chapter 2 there; nevertheless if he peeled their pitch they are permitted, etc. ; see there]; and likewise in Sefat Emet explicitly; and the Rosh there on "but we learned," etc. ; thus, etc.; and likewise in the Rosh chapter 2 seif 1; and there is no distinction between there was pitch and it was peeled and between there was never pitch, as proven below in the last chapter, etc. ; see there; and likewise in Sefat Emet and in Tosafot there; and in many places there it says "and R. concedes," etc. "and what is the difference," etc.; and perforce in jars that are not pitched, where it says "and he concedes," etc. "and what," etc.; and if it were so, also for the Rabbis it would be difficult ; what is the difference, etc. And this "trodden in" must be beforehand; and in earthenware and wood and stone as above; and see siman 135 seif 4 that even in other earthenware vessels whose beginning of use is by a gentile, iruy is required.

And if its initial use, etc. This is Rava's first version, as stated in the aforementioned Tosafot. Sefer HaTerumah and Rashba likewise rule this way. See Rosh, seif 33: ‘one may further say,’ etc., and Tosafot 72b, s.v. im, etc.
If it is wooden. There is no distinction between wood and stone except where they are pitched. See Rashi on the mishnah there, s.v. veshel etz, etc., and Rosh, perek 2, seif 22.

But, etc. In Torah HaBayit; and nevertheless even the Sages did not require filling and iruy in earthenware except at the beginning of its use in a gentile's hand, etc.; but at the beginning of its use in a Jew's hand, wiping-dry suffices ; and this is what Machatz wrote, etc. "of idolaters" ; for otherwise why does it teach "of idolaters"; and so said Raavad z"l ; end; and nevertheless specifically when they are not pitched, for in pitched ones there is no distinction as above.

(Extract) But, etc. requires wiping-dry ; this is Raavad's view; but Ran disagrees there and wrote: from what the mishnah teaches anonymously "forbidden," it implies even if the beginning of its use is by Israel; and that which the braita teaches "of idolatry" is to include that nevertheless R. permits; and all this is for the Rif's version; but for Tosafot's version who wrote Shulchan Aruch ; end ; the mishnah [deals with] at the beginning of use by Israel; and it requires study (end).

(Extract) But if it is earthenware it requires wiping-dry ; it requires study, for the mishnah [deals with] at the beginning of its use by Israel, as Tosafot wrote and as above; and even when it is not pitched it is forbidden, as stated "even though he peeled," etc.; and the same applies when it is not pitched as above; and even though Tosafot wrote "and one can say the mishnah," etc. ; for a temporary matter or many times; nevertheless from the Tur's language, who distinguishes between its beginning by a gentile or by Israel, it implies he explains Tosafot's answer in such a case; and even though in Torah HaBayit he wrote thus ; that was according to the version that does not have the first version, and Tosafot's answer is not needed; but for us it is difficult. And as the Rosh wrote that wiping-dry does not help for earthenware, as above; and it is not comparable to a cover that they distinguished in chapter 2 (one version 2) between the beginning of their use in a Jew's hand, etc. ; for there they are not constantly occupied with wine abundantly as in a winepress, as Ran wrote; therefore even wiping-dry is not required; but here in all cases iruy is required (end).

segments.he: היא כו' בין כו'. פשוט בכמה מקומות וכמ"ש לקמן:
segments.en: It is, etc., whether, etc. This is clear from several places, as will be stated below.

segments.he: אלא בשל כו'. כר"ע וכסתם מתני' נ"א ב':
segments.en: And its appurtenances, etc. There on 52a Rav Huna asks, etc.: ‘If we say,’ etc., ‘rather,’ etc.

segments.he: ותשמישיה כו'. שם נ"ב א' בעי ר"ה כו' אילימא כו' ואלא כו' וקי"ל כר"ע כנ"ל וה"ה לנויה דבכלל תשמישה הוא וזה דפריך משמשי כו' ולא מוקי בנויה:
segments.en: We rule like Rabbi Akiva, as above. The same applies to its ornaments, for they are included among its appurtenances. This is why the Gemara challenges from appurtenances, etc., and does not answer by distinguishing ornaments.

segments.he: ותקרובתה כו'. ר"ל ג"כ אינה אסורה מיד וכמש"ש מ"ד ב' וערש"י שם ד"ה שאין הקדש כו':
segments.en: And its offering, etc. Meaning its offering is also not forbidden immediately, as written below seif 2, and as Rashi there explains in the passage "for sacred offerings, etc."

segments.he: ועשה כו'. עס"ג:
segments.en: And he made, etc. See seif 3.

segments.he: ישראל כו'. גמ' שם מ"ו א' נ"ג ב':
segments.en: A Jew, etc. The Gemara there, 46a and 53b.

en_segments: It is, etc., whether, etc. This is clear from several places, as will be stated below.
And its appurtenances, etc. There on 52a Rav Huna asks, etc.: ‘If we say,’ etc., ‘rather,’ etc.

We rule like Rabbi Akiva, as above. The same applies to its ornaments, for they are included among its appurtenances. This is why the Gemara challenges from appurtenances, etc., and does not answer by distinguishing ornaments.
And its offering, etc. Meaning its offering is also not forbidden immediately, as written below seif 2, and as Rashi there explains in the passage "for sacred offerings, etc."
And he made, etc. See seif 3.
A Jew, etc. The Gemara there, 46a and 53b.

segments.he: כל הצלמים כו' דסתמא לשם אלילים כו' דודאי לנוי נעשו כו'. איכא למידק דיוקא דרישא אדסיפא דברישא קאמר דמסתמא כו' הא בספק מותרים ובסיפא קאמר דודאי כו' הא בספק אסורים ונראה דברישא קושטא דמלתא קאמר דמסתמ' דרכי הכפרים שלא לעשות לנוי אלא לשם אלילים ואה"נ בספק אם נעשו לשם אלילים או לנוי אסורים דבעינן דוקא למידע בודאי שנעשו לשם נוי כדקאמר בסיפא וכן מוכח בטור עיין שם וכן דעת הפרישה והב"ח בקונטרס אחרון השיג עליו ולפמ"ש דבריו נכונים וגם תימה על הב"ח דבש"ס דף מ"א ע"ב גבי הא דאמרינן התם אלא אימא הא צלמים עצמם אסורים סתמא כרבי מאיר כו' מוכח כולה סוגיא דבצלמים עצמם הנמצאים בשוק לא אמרינן אימר בטלום כיון דשלימים הם עיין שם ודוק:
segments.en: All images, etc., because ordinarily they are made for idolatry, etc.; for certainly they were made for ornament, etc. There is an apparent contradiction between the implication of the first clause and the latter clause. The first clause says that ordinarily, etc., implying that where there is doubt they are permitted, while the latter clause says that certainly, etc., implying that where there is doubt they are forbidden. It appears that the first clause merely states the actual ordinary circumstance, namely that in villages images are ordinarily not made for decoration but for idolatry. In truth, where there is doubt whether they were made for idolatry or for decoration they are forbidden, because one must know with certainty that they were made for decoration, as stated in the latter clause. This is also evident from the Tur. See there. This is likewise the view of the Prisha. The Bach, in Kuntres Acharon, challenged him, but according to what I have written his words are correct. It is also astonishing that the Bach did not note that in the Gemara, daf 41b, concerning the statement, 'Rather say: the images themselves are ordinarily forbidden, in accordance with R' Meir,' etc., the entire discussion proves that regarding intact images found in the marketplace we do not say that perhaps they were nullified, since they remain whole. See there and examine carefully.

segments.he: המדינה. פירוש עיר וכן מצינו הרבה פעמים בלשון הש"ס והפוסקים:
segments.en: The province. Meaning a city; and so we find many times in the language of the Gemara and the poskim.

segments.he: והיה ביד הצורה כו'. המחבר העתיק מלשון הרמב"ם כדרכו ומשמע מלשון זה דכל צורות העומדות על פתח המדינה ובידם מקל כו' אסורים וכן משמע קצת מהגהת הרב בסעיף ד' ע"ש וכן בב"י תמה על מה שמשמע מהטור דלא אסור בכה"ג אלא צורת אדם דווקא (ולי אפשר דהטור ל"ד נקט אדם ומפני זה לא כתב האי דינא בריש הסי' דהתם עיקר דוכתא דהאי דינא ע"ש ודוק) והב"ח כתב ודלא כמ"ש בש"ע והיה ביד הצורה וכו' דליתא אלא דווקא בצורת אדם עכ"ל ותימה איך חלק על הרמב"ם (וכמדומה שלא ידע שדברי המחבר מועתקים מהרמב"ם) והמחבר בלי ראיה כלל בפרט להקל וכ"ש שאפשר לפרש גם דברי הטור כן ע"ש גם פשטא דסוגיית הש"ס משמע כן ע"ש:
segments.en: And it was in the hand of the form etc. The mechaber copied from Rambam's language as is his custom; it implies from this language that all forms standing at the city entrance with a staff etc. in their hand are forbidden; and so somewhat appears from the Rav's glosses in seif 4 — see there; and so in Beit Yosef he wonders at what appears from the Tur that only human form specifically is forbidden in such a case (and possibly the Tur did not specifically mean human, and for this reason did not write this law at the beginning of the siman where it primarily belongs — see there — investigate); and the Bach wrote unlike what the Shulchan Aruch wrote “and it was in the hand of the form” etc. — it does not exist; rather specifically in human form — end; and it is wondrous how he disputes the Rambam (and apparently did not know the mechaber's words are copied from Rambam) and the mechaber without any proof at all, especially to be lenient; and all the more since the Tur's words can also be explained that way — see there; and also the plain Gemara sugya appears so — see there.

segments.he: צורת מקל או צפור כו'. עיין ר"פ כל הצלמים מפרש בש"ס דכל הנך מראים שנעשו לשם אליל ונראה בזמנינו הכל לפי ענין ובין בכרכים ובין בכפרים הכל מה שמראים הדברים שנעשו לשם אליל או לנוי:
segments.en: Form of a staff or a bird etc. See beginning of chapter "all images" — explained in the Gemara that all these indicate they were made for idolatry; and it appears in our time everything depends on the matter, whether in cities or villages — all according to what the things indicate as made for idolatry or for ornament.

segments.he: דינו כדין צלם. פי' כדין צלם שיש בו הוכחה שנעשה לשם אליל ואסור בלא ביטול וע"ד שיתבאר בסי' קמ"ו ע"ש:
segments.en: Its law is like that of an image. Meaning: like the law of an image for which there is proof it was made for idolatry — forbidden without nullification; and in the manner explained in siman 146 — see there.

segments.he: אבל אותן שתולין בצואר כו'. היינו בידוע שלא השתחוה לו (ואתא לאשמועינן דל"ת כיון שתולין אותו בצואר מיד נאסר) הא לאו הכי לא גרע מאם מצא כלים שעליהם צורת עבודת כוכבי' דהכלים אסורים אם הם מכובדים דכיון שדרך לעבוד אותה הצורה חיישינן שמא נעבדו הכלים כדלקמן סעיף ג' והכי נמי איכא למיחש להכי ובעובד כוכבים עצמו אין לחלק בין מכובד לבזוי דדווקא בכלים אמרי' דעל המבוזים ודאי לנוי הכלי נעשו מה שאין כן הכא ומצאתי בהר"ן פרק כל הצלמים וז"ל כתב הרשב"א דבזמן הזה שחוקקים חקק בכלים ומציירים בהם צורות ודמות עבודת כוכבים אף המוצא אותם הכלים אסורים ע"כ וצל"ע שאפשר שאין עובדים היום לצורות הללו אלא לזכר בעלמא עושין אותם עכ"ל הר"ן וכ"כ רבינו ירוחם נתי"ז ח"ד ואפשר דעובדי כוכבים אלו שאין אדוקים בעבודת כוכבים כל מה שעושין בצורות הללו בכלים אינם עושים אלא לנוי ומותרים בהנאה כלם ואסור להשהותן משום חשד אם הם בולטים וראוי להחמיר בספק איסור תורה ע"כ ואפשר בצורה עצמו כיון שדרך שמשתחוים לו לכ"ע אסור:
segments.en: But those hung on the neck etc. Meaning when it is known he did not bow to it (and comes to teach one should not think that since they hang it on the neck it is immediately forbidden) — if not so, it is no better than when one finds vessels upon which are idolatrous forms: the vessels are forbidden if they are honored, since there is a customary way to worship that form we are concerned perhaps the vessels were worshipped, as below seif 3; and here too there is room for such concern. Regarding the gentile himself there is no distinction between honored and dishonored — specifically regarding vessels we say that dishonored ones were certainly made for vessel ornamentation, which is not the case here. I found in the Ran chapter "all images": Rashba wrote that nowadays when they engrave carvings in vessels and paint on them forms and images of idolatry, even one who finds those vessels they are forbidden — end; and wonder, for perhaps they do not worship those forms nowadays but make them merely as a memorial — end Ran; and so R. Yerucham 17:4; and possibly these gentiles who are not attached to idolatry, all they do with these forms on vessels is done only for ornament and permitted for benefit; and forbidden to leave them because of suspicion if they are protruding; and proper to be stringent in a doubtful Torah prohibition — end; and possibly regarding the form itself, since there is a customary way to bow to it — forbidden according to all.

segments.he: מי שהיה ביתו סמוך כו'. משמע מדברי הט"ו שאפילו אין הבית עצמו נעבד אסור לבנות כותל להבית כיון שמהנה לאליל וכן משמע פשטא דמתניתין וכן מוכח מדברי רש"י פ"ק דעבודת כוכבים (דף ט"ז ע"א) שפירש אמאי דתנן התם בונים עמהם בימסאות וז"ל בימסאות בנין שאינו לצורך עבודת כוכבים ומקריב זבחים דהוי תשמיש דתשמיש לעבודת כוכבים עכ"ל ומביאו הטור בסמוך משמע הא תשמיש דעבודת כוכבים עצמה אסור ואם כן הבית שהעבודת כוכבים בתוכו הוא תשמיש דעבודת כוכבים ממש ואסור והיינו דאסרינן כיפה שמעמידין בה עבודת כוכבים משום שהוא תשמיש עבודת כוכבים וכדאי' בש"ס והב"ח כתב וז"ל ומפרש במשנה פרק כל הצלמים מי שהיה ביתו סמוך לאליל נראה שאם לא היה הבית עצמו נעבד אלא שהעמידו בו עבודת כוכבים לא היה נקרא מהנה לעבודת כוכבים בבנין הכותל ותו דהא מותר לבנות טרקלין שיהא העובד כוכבים מעמיד בה כיפה להעמיד בה עבודת כוכבים לרש"י עד כאן לשונו ולא ירדתי לסוף דעתו דאדרבה משם ראיה דהא דוקא בטרקלין דהוי תשמיש דתשמיש שרי רש"י הא לאו הכי לא ואם כן למה יהא מותר לבנות כותל לבית שמעמידין בה עבודת כוכבים ומ"ש רש"י שהבית עצמו נעבד אין כוונתו כמו שהבין הב"ח אלא רצה לו' משום דקתני בסיפא אבניו ועציו ואפרה מטמאים כשרץ (פירש"י אינו מטמא במשא) ר' עקיבא אומר כנדה (מטמא במשא) ואי לא היה הבית עצמו נעבד אלא הוי משמשי אליל לא הוי אמר ר"ע כנדה דהכי אמרינן להדיא ר"פ ר"ע אהא מתניתין ולר"ע למאי הלכתא אתקש לשרץ למשמשיה דלא מטמאין במשא ע"ש תראה דמ"ש הוא ברור גם בדרישה פי' דברי רש"י בע"א ואין לשון רש"י מורה כפירושו (ומ"ש התוספות וכ"פ הקונטרס הוא שבמ"ש והבית עצמו נעבד ממילא מיושב קושייתם) ומ"ש הוא ברור:
segments.en: One whose house was adjacent, etc. The words of the Tur and Shulchan Aruch imply that even if the house itself is not worshipped, it is forbidden to build a wall for the house because he thereby benefits the idolatry. This is likewise the plain meaning of the Mishnah and is also proven from Rashi at the beginning of Avodah Zarah, daf 16a. On the Mishnah there, which states that one may build with them bathhouses, Rashi explains: 'Bathhouses are buildings not themselves for idolatry, while the sacrifices offered there are only an appurtenance of an appurtenance of idolatry.' The Tur cites this below. This implies that an actual appurtenance of idolatry is forbidden. Thus a house in which idolatry is placed is an actual appurtenance of idolatry and is forbidden. This is why a dome in which idolatry is set up is forbidden, because it is an appurtenance of idolatry, as stated in the Gemara. The Bach writes that the Mishnah in the chapter Kol HaTzelamim, 'one whose house was adjacent to idolatry,' appears to mean that if the house itself were not worshipped but merely contained idolatry, building its wall would not be considered benefiting idolatry. He further argues that according to Rashi one may build a palace in which the non-Jew will place a dome containing idolatry. End of his words. I do not understand his reasoning. On the contrary, that is a proof against him, because Rashi permits specifically a palace, which is only an appurtenance of an appurtenance. Otherwise it would be forbidden. Why then should it be permitted to build a wall for a house in which idolatry is placed? As for Rashi's statement that the house itself is worshipped, his intent is not as the Bach understood. Rather, it addresses the latter clause of the Mishnah: 'its stones, wood, and dust convey impurity like a sheretz; R' Akiva says like a niddah.' If the house itself were not worshipped but merely served as an appurtenance of idolatry, R' Akiva would not say that it is like a niddah. So the Gemara explicitly states at the beginning of the chapter R' Akiva: according to R' Akiva, for what law is it compared to a sheretz? For its appurtenances, which do not convey impurity by carrying. See there. This makes my explanation clear. The Prisha explains Rashi differently, but Rashi's wording does not support his explanation. The words of Tosafos, 'and so Rashi explained,' refer to the fact that by saying the house itself is worshipped, Rashi thereby resolves their question. What I have written is clear.

segments.he: כונס לתוך שלו. ד' אמות כן הוא במשנה וטור ופוסקים:
segments.en: He enters within his own. Four cubits — so it is in the Mishnah, Tur, and poskim.

segments.he: שלו מותר בהנאה. וחלקו עולה לו שאם היה עביו של כותל ב' אמות מונה האמה שלו וכונס עוד ג' אמות לתוך שלו. רש"י והר"ן:
segments.en: His portion is permitted for benefit. And his portion is counted for him — if the wall’s thickness is two cubits, he counts one cubit as his and enters a further three cubits within his own — Rashi and the Ran.

segments.he: הבית עצמו נעבד. דאל"כ אלא להעמיד בו אליל הא קי"ל משמשי אליל אינם נאסרים עד שיעבדו אבל אם הוא עצמו נעבד שפי' נאסר דקיימא לן ר"ס קל"ט בעובד כוכבים נאסר מיד ומ"ש בטור כאן אם הוא של ישראל וכו' ר"ל שעל כל פנים עובד כוכבים עשאו אלא שמכרו אחר כך לישראל אבל אם ישראל עשאו לא נאסר עד שיעבד כ"כ ב"י וראיתי מאן דמוקי לה כאן בישראל מומר דהוי כעובד כוכבים בזה והבל יפצה פיהו דדינו כישראל בזה ולכל עונשי' שבתורה כמ"ש ר"ס קל"ט וכתב הר"ן אע"ג דגבי אילן אינו נאסר לעיל ר"ס זה אם השתחוה לו ולא אמרינן דהוה תלוש ולבסוף חברו דשאני אילן ששרשיו מחוברין מאד בקרקע וחשבינן ליה כמחובר מעיקרא בפ"ק דחולין ורש"י פי' דבאילן מיירי שלא נטע יחור אלא גרעין אבל בנטע יחור הוה באמת תלוש ולבסוף חברו והוי תלוש:
segments.en: The house itself is worshipped. For otherwise, if it merely serves as a place in which to set up idolatry, we rule that appurtenances of idolatry do not become forbidden until they are actually used. But if the house itself is worshipped, it becomes forbidden immediately, because we rule at the beginning of siman 139 that idolatry belonging to a non-Jew becomes forbidden immediately. What the Tur writes here, 'if it belongs to a Jew,' etc., means that in any event a non-Jew made it and later sold it to a Jew. But if a Jew made it, it does not become forbidden until it is worshipped. So wrote the Beit Yosef. I saw someone explain the case here as involving an apostate Jew, whose status in this matter would be like that of a non-Jew. His statement is utterly mistaken, for in this respect and for all punishments of the Torah his status remains that of a Jew, as written at the beginning of siman 139. The Ran writes that although regarding a tree it does not become forbidden, as above at the beginning of this siman, merely because one bowed to it, and we do not say it was originally detached and later attached, a tree is different because its roots are strongly attached to the ground and it is considered attached from the outset, as stated at the beginning of Chullin. Rashi explains that the case of a tree concerns one planted from a seed, but if one planted a cutting, it is in fact detached and later attached and is treated as detached property.

segments.he: וכיידו. פירוש צר בו צורות:
segments.en: and he designated it. Meaning: he drew images on it.

segments.he: נוטל מה שחידש. פי' הישראל אבל עובד כוכבים אין צריך ליטול הכל אלא בכל דהו סגי. ב"י בשם הר"ן:
segments.en: He removes what was renewed. Meaning: Israel removes; but a gentile does not need to remove everything — any small amount suffices. In the name of the Ran.

segments.he: אסור. משום דאזיל ומודה לפני אליל ביום חגו:
segments.en: Forbidden. Because he goes and gives thanks before an idol on its festival day.

segments.he: דבר המתקיים. עד יום חגו דחזי ליה קמיה ביום חגו ואזיל ומודי. רש"י:
segments.en: A thing that endures. Until its festival day — that he sees it before him on the festival day and goes and gives thanks — Rashi.

segments.he: ואם היא מלוה ברבית כו'. והתוספות כתבו סתמא דבמלוה במשכון נמי הוה כמציל מידם שכמה פעמים אובדות אפילו במשכון עד כאן לשונו וכב"י דנראה שטעמא מפני שהלואות דהאידנא הם ברבית ולי נראה שטעמא מפני דהאידנא ידם תקיפה עלינו ובקל יכול העובד כוכבים להעליל ולכפור סך ההלואה וכיוצא בזה וכן משמע בעט"ז ע"ש מיהו בזמן הזה בכל ענין שרי מהנך טעמי דלקמן ס"ס זה וכ"כ רבינו ירוחם:
segments.en: And if it is a loan with interest, etc. Tosafos write without qualification that even a loan secured by collateral is considered rescuing property from their hands, because many times such loans are lost despite the collateral. End of their words. The Beit Yosef writes that the reason appears to be that contemporary loans are made with interest. It appears to me, however, that the reason is that nowadays their power over us is strong, and a non-Jew can easily fabricate a claim and deny the amount of the loan and the like. This is likewise implied by Olat Tamid. See there. In any event, nowadays the transaction is permitted in every manner for the reasons stated below at the end of this siman. Rabbeinu Yerucham likewise writes this.

segments.he: הולכים ליריד כו'. כתב הטור בשם הרא"ש דאפילו ביום חגם שרי משום דדלמא לא משכח ליה אלא ביריד והוה ליה דבר האבוד וכתב הר"ן דהיינו דוקא בדברים שצריך להם לעצמו אבל להשתכר בהן לא דהנאת ריוח לא מקרי דבר האבוד ומביאו ב"י וד"מ מיהו כל זה מדינא אבל האידנא הכל שרי כמ"ש הרא"ש וטור ושאר פוסקים דלאו עובדי עבודת כוכבים הן וכדלעיל ס"ס קמ"ח ולקמן סעיף ד' וכ"כ הב"ח ס"ס זה דהאידנא אין חוששין לשום דבר ונהגו היתר אף ביריד ביום אידם ואפילו נותנים מכס לכומרים:
segments.en: Forbidden. For he benefits from the customs exemption they give him — Tur and Ran; and the Bach ruled this is specifically regarding individuals, but when they grant freedom equally to all people there is no prohibition; but if they give the customs exemption only when one places a crown on his head in honor of idolatry — even if they give to all people it is forbidden — see there where he elaborated; and see above siman 143.

segments.he: אסור. שהרי נהנה שמנחת לו המכס. טור והר"ן. ופסק הב"ח דהיינו דוקא ביחידים אבל כשעושים חירות לכל אדם בשוה אין בזה איסור אבל אם אין מניחין המכס אלא כשמניח עטרה בראשו לכבוד עבודת כוכבים אפילו מניחין לכל אדם אסור ע"ש שהאריך וע"ל סי' קמ"ג:
segments.en: He brings them to the Dead Sea.

segments.he: יוליכם ליה"מ. ובהניחו המכס ליחיד דאסור משום שנהנה נראה מדברי הב"ח דסגי בהולכת הנאת המכס ליה"מ וע"ש:
segments.en: And in the case where the customs exemption is given to an individual — which is forbidden because he benefits — it appears from the Bach's words that it suffices to send the benefit of the customs to the Dead Sea; see there.

segments.he: שלא למכור. כגון במקום שחשודים על הרביעה כן הוא בש"ס (עבודת כוכבים סוף דף י"ד) ורש"י ותוס' וכל הפוסקים דלא כהעט"ז שנעלם ממנו זה וכתב הטעם שאותן המקומות אסרו בהמה דקה משום שבית' אטו בהמה גסה וזהו גזירה לגזירה שהרי בהמה גסה גופה גזירה רחוקה היא כדלקמן גם כל הסוגיא לא אזלה לדידיה ע"ש. שוב מצאתי ברש"י וברטנורה פרק מקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נ"ג ע"א) שכתבו כהעט"ז ותמהני וצ"ע בתוספות שם דף י"ד ד"ה אמר רב כו':
segments.en: Not to sell. For example where they are suspected of bestiality — so it is in the Gemara (Avodah Zarah end of page 14) and Rashi, Tosafot, and all the poskim — unlike the Eliyah Rabba to whom this was hidden, who wrote the reason that in those places they forbade small animals because of slaughtering them on account of large animals — and this is a decree upon a decree, for large animals themselves are already a distant decree as below; also the entire sugya does not go according to him — see there. I then found in Rashi and the Bartenura chapter Makom SheNahagu (Pesachim 53a) who wrote like the Eliyah Rabba — and I am astonished; and the matter requires investigation in Tosafot there page 14 s.v. amar Rav etc.

segments.he: בהמה גסה כו'. גזרה מכירה אטו שאלה או שכירות ובשאלה או שכירות אסור לפי שהעובד כוכבים עושה מלאכה בשבת בבהמתו של ישראל שהוא מצווה על שביתת בהמתו כדכתיב לא תעשה כל מלאכה וגו' וכל בהמתך אי נמי גזרה שלפעמים ימכרנה בע"ש סמוך לחשכה ואמר ליה נסייה ניהלה ושמעה לקליה ואזלה מחמתיה והוה ליה מחמר אחר בהמתו בשבת:
segments.en: Large animal etc. A decree: selling because of lending or renting; and in lending or renting it is forbidden because the gentile performs labor on Shabbat with the Israelite’s animal, and he is commanded regarding his animal’s rest as written "you shall not do any labor" etc. "and all your animals"; alternatively, a decree because sometimes he will sell it on Friday evening close to dark and say to him "try it out" — and it heeds his voice and goes on account of him, making him one who drives his animal on Shabbat.

segments.he: סרסור. ישראל דלא שייך ביה הני טעמי:
segments.en: Broker. An Israelite — these reasons do not apply to him.

segments.he: ועכשיו כו'. לפי שבימיהם היו דרים הרבה יהודים ביחד והיו יכולין למכור זה לזה אבל האידנא שמעט יהודים דרים במקום אחד ואי לא מזבני איכא פסידא. טור והפוסקים. ויש פוסקים כתבו הטעם לפי שעתה אין אנו בקיאין בקלא דניחוש דשמעה לקליה כו' ומשום שאלה ושכירות ליכא למיחש דאין רגילין עכשיו לקנות בהמה כדי להשכירה כי אם לצורך עצמו קונהו ע"כ וכתב הר"ן דלפי זה אפילו לקנות כדי להרויח למכרה מותר ע"כ וכן נראה דעת המחבר וכן נהגו וכ"כ העט"ז וכתב עוד הר"ן ואעפ"כ בעל נפש ימעט אבל בשאלה שהדבר פשוט לאסור ראוי למחות למי שעושה כך ע"כ ועיין בא"ח סימן רמ"ו וכל זה בבהמה טמאה אבל בטהורה כתב סה"ת ופוסקים דא"צ לכל זה די"ל דלשחיטה לוקחה וכמ"ש רש"י:
segments.en: And nowadays, etc. The reason is that in their days many Jews lived together and could sell to one another, whereas nowadays only a few Jews live in one place and, if they cannot sell, they will suffer a loss. Tur and the poskim. Some poskim give another reason: nowadays we are not sufficiently expert regarding the animal's voice to be concerned that the non-Jew will hear it, etc. There is likewise no concern regarding lending or renting animals, because nowadays people do not ordinarily purchase an animal in order to rent it out, but purchase it for their own use. According to this, the Ran writes that even purchasing in order to profit by reselling is permitted. So appears to be the Mechaber's view, and this is the accepted custom. Olat Tamid likewise writes this. The Ran further writes that nevertheless a person of piety should minimize such dealings. But regarding lending an animal, where the prohibition is clear, one should protest against anyone who does so. See Orach Chayyim, siman 246. All of this concerns a non-kosher animal. Regarding a kosher animal, Sefer HaTerumah and the poskim write that none of these considerations is needed, because one can say that the non-Jew purchases it for slaughter, as Rashi wrote.

segments.he: ואפילו אם היא מומחית. כלומר ולא אמרינן דלא מרעת נפשה כדלקמן סימן קנ"ה ברופא מומחה ב"י וכ"כ הפרישה וב"ח וכתב הטעם דמיילדת יכולה לומר נפל היה וכה"ג ותמיה לי דבירושלמי פרק אין מעמידין קאמר כי היכי דברופא אומן מותר ה"ה במיילדת חכמה וכן בשום פוסק לא נזכר דבמיילדת מומח' אסור וצ"ע:
segments.en: Even if she is an expert. Meaning: we do not say she will not harm herself, as below in siman 155 regarding an expert physician — Beit Yosef; and so Perishah and Bach; he wrote the reason that a midwife can say it was a stillbirth and the like.

segments.he: ואפי' אחרים בו'. אמיילדת נמי קאי:
segments.en: And I wonder, for in the Jerusalem Talmud chapter Ein Ma'amidim it says: just as an expert physician is permitted, so too an expert midwife; and furthermore no posek mentioned that an expert midwife is forbidden — and the matter requires investigation.

segments.he: בשאר איסורי הנאה מתרפאין כו':
segments.en: From other benefit-prohibitions one may be healed etc.

segments.he: שלא כדרך הנאתן כו'. לצורך רפואה אבל שלא לצורך רפואה אפי' שלא כדרך הנאתן אסור הרא"ש פרק כל שעה ופשוט הוא והיינו באיסורי הנאה אבל באיסורי אכילה שרי כדאי' בפוסקים:
segments.en: Not in the normal manner of enjoyment etc. For medicinal purposes; but not for medicinal purposes, even not in the normal manner of enjoyment is forbidden — the Rosh chapter Kol Sha'ah; and it is simple; and this is regarding benefit-prohibitions, but eating-prohibitions are permitted — as stated by the poskim.

segments.he: מותר להתרפאות כו'. ובלבד שלא יאכל וישתה האיסור. שם. וכ"כ הרב בסמוך והיינו דוקא כדרך אכילתן אבל שלא כדרך אכילתן כ' המרדכי ואגודה ר"פ כ"ש בשם ראבי"ה דמותר. וכתב עוד המרדכי שם דמהאי טעמא מותר לאכול חלב חי ומיהו אדם בריא יזהר ע"כ ועיין בתשו' ר"א ן' חיים סי' קי"ב:
segments.en: It is permitted to be healed etc. Provided one does not eat or drink the forbidden matter — there; and so the Rav wrote nearby; and that is specifically in the normal manner of eating; but not in the normal manner of eating — the Mordechai and Agudah at the beginning of the chapter Kol She’hu in the name of Ra’avyah wrote it is permitted; and the Mordechai further wrote there that for this reason it is permitted to eat raw fat; however a healthy person should be careful — end; and see responsum R. Eliyahu ibn Chayim siman 112.

segments.he: אפילו חולי כו'. אפי' דרך הנאתן:
segments.en: Even illness etc. Even in the normal manner of enjoyment.

segments.he: בזמן הזה. כלו' דעובדי כוכבים בזמן הזה לאו עובדי עבודת כוכבים הן וכדלעיל סימן קכ"ג וקכ"ד וכמה דוכתי והרשב"א דאוסר בתשובה (והביאו ב"י ר"ס קכ"ג) לעשות מרחץ מסתם יינם מיירי לדין הש"ס וכ"כ הריב"ש סי' נ"ה דסתם יינם דינו כדין עצי עבודת כוכבים והיינו לדין הש"ס ונ"מ במקום שהגוים שם עובדי עבודת כוכבים הן:
segments.en: Nowadays. Meaning that gentiles nowadays are not idolaters, as above siman 123 and 124 and many other places; and the Rashba who forbids in a responsum (brought by Beit Yosef beginning of siman 123) making a bath from their ordinary wine — he deals with the Gemara's law; and so the Rivash siman 55 wrote that ordinary wine has the same law as wood of idolatry — and that is by the Gemara's law; and it is relevant where the gentiles there are idolaters.

segments.he: ולעשות ממנו מרחץ לחולה. אבל לבריא לא דסיכה בכלל שתיה או"ה שם:
segments.en: And to make a bath from it for a sick person. But not for a healthy person — for anointing is included in drinking — Or Zarua there.

segments.he: דמותר לזלף כו'. ע"ל ס"ס ק"ח ס"ק (י') [כ"ה]:
segments.en: That it is permitted to sprinkle etc. See above end of siman 108 s.k. 25.

segments.he: או שאר דבר איסור. אפי' הוא מאיסורי הנאה דקי"ל כל הנשרפין אפרן מותר חוץ מעצי עבודת כוכבים ויי"נ ריב"ש סי' רכ"ה וכן נראה דעת הרב:
segments.en: Or other forbidden matter.

segments.he: הרפואה ידועה כו'. עיין בא"ח סי' שכ"ח ותרי"ח:
segments.en: Even if it is from benefit-prohibitions — for we rule that all that is burned its ashes are permitted, except for wood of idolatry and yayin nesech — Rivash siman 225; and so appears the Rav's view.

en_segments: From other benefit-prohibitions one may be healed etc.

Not in the normal manner of enjoyment etc. For medicinal purposes; but not for medicinal purposes, even not in the normal manner of enjoyment is forbidden — the Rosh chapter Kol Sha'ah; and it is simple; and this is regarding benefit-prohibitions, but eating-prohibitions are permitted — as stated by the poskim.

It is permitted to be healed etc. Provided one does not eat or drink the forbidden matter — there; and so the Rav wrote nearby; and that is specifically in the normal manner of eating; but not in the normal manner of eating — the Mordechai and Agudah at the beginning of the chapter Kol She’hu in the name of Ra’avyah wrote it is permitted; and the Mordechai further wrote there that for this reason it is permitted to eat raw fat; however a healthy person should be careful — end; and see responsum R. Eliyahu ibn Chayim siman 112.
Even illness etc. Even in the normal manner of enjoyment.

Nowadays. Meaning that gentiles nowadays are not idolaters, as above siman 123 and 124 and many other places; and the Rashba who forbids in a responsum (brought by Beit Yosef beginning of siman 123) making a bath from their ordinary wine — he deals with the Gemara's law; and so the Rivash siman 55 wrote that ordinary wine has the same law as wood of idolatry — and that is by the Gemara's law; and it is relevant where the gentiles there are idolaters.
And to make a bath from it for a sick person. But not for a healthy person — for anointing is included in drinking — Or Zarua there.
That it is permitted to sprinkle etc. See above end of siman 108 s.k. 25.
Or other forbidden matter.
Even if it is from benefit-prohibitions — for we rule that all that is burned its ashes are permitted, except for wood of idolatry and yayin nesech — Rivash siman 225; and so appears the Rav's view.
notes: Existing English was preserved where it covered the Hebrew; missing Hebrew slots were freshly translated and merged blobs were split only at textual boundaries.

segments.he: חוץ כו'. שם בסנהדרין ואע"ג דר' ישמעאל פליג קי"ל כר' יוחנן דאמר נמנו וגמרו וכ"ה הסוגיא בפ"ב דפסחים ובפ"ב דכתובות (י"ט א') ובפ' בתרא דיומא וש"מ:
segments.en: Except, etc. There in Sanhedrin; and although R. Yishmael disagrees we rule like R. Yochanan who said they counted and concluded; and so the sugya in chapter 2 of Pesachim and chapter 2 of Ketubot (19a) and the last chapter of Yoma ; learn from this.

segments.he: אם הוא בצנעה כו'. גמ' שם:
segments.en: If he is in private, etc. Gemara there.

segments.he: ואם ירצה כו'. כמ"ש ברפי"ט דשבת כל מצוה שמסרו כו' ואלישע בעל בנפים בפ"ד (ורפי"ט) דשבת ור"ע וריב"ב וכל הרוגי מלכות שמסרו עצמן על מצות פרטיות ואמרינן בשוחר טוב מה המכות האלה בין ידיך ואמר אשר הכיתי בית מאהבי המכות האלה גרמו לי ליאהב לאבי שבשמים מה לך יוצא ליסקל על ששמרתי את השבת מה לך יוצא לישרף על שאכלתי את המצה מה לך יוצא ליהרג על שמלתי את בני כו' ובפסחים נ"ג ב' מה ראו כו' ועתוס' שם בד"ה מה. ומפר"ת דצלם כו' והרמב"ם אוסר ומפרש דכל הנ"ל בשעה צריכה לכך וכמ"ש בנ"י בסנהדרין שם ובחנניה מישאל ועזריה בלא"ה ל"ק דפרהסיא אפילו אערקתא דמסאנא כו' וכ"כ תוס' בכתובות ל"ג ב' אבל מ"מ אינו מיושב דשם להנאתו ודניאל שמסר עצמו על התפלה בביתו ועוד הביא הרא"ש ראיה שם בעבודת כוכבים מירושלמי ר' אבא בר זימנא הוה חייט אצל עובד כוכבים וא"ל אכול נבילות ואי לא קטילנא לך א"ל אי בעית למקטיל קטול דלא אכילנא ומסתמא בצנעה היה בביתו של עובד כוכבים אלא שרי"ו כתב דוקא כשהעובד כוכבים מתכוין להעביר על דת וכן מיירי ההיא דירושלמי וכן ההיא דדניאל אבל דחנניה מישאל ועזריה לא משמע כן כנ"ל ומתוס' משמע כדברי רי"ו שכתבו בעבודת כוכבים כ"ז ב' סד"ה יכול. ואם רצה להחמיר כו' כמו ר' אבא כו' ובסנהדרין ע"ד ב' ד"ה קטול כ' ההוא עובדא כו' משום דלהנאתו היה כמ"ש תוס' שם ועבר"ן פ"ד דשבת:
segments.en: And if he wishes, etc. As stated in end of chapter 19 of Shabbat ; every mitzvah they handed over, etc.; and Elisha ba'al kenafayim in chapter 4 (end) of Shabbat; and R. Akiva and R. Yehudah ben Bava and all martyrs of the kingdom who gave themselves for private mitzvot; and we say in Shochar Tov ; what are these wounds between your hands; and he said those who struck me in my lovers' house ; these wounds caused me to love my Father in heaven; why do you go out to be stoned for keeping Shabbat, to be burned for eating matzah, to be killed for circumcising my son, etc.; and in Pesachim 53b ; what did they see, etc.; and Tosafot there s.v. mah. And from Rabbenu Chananel ; image, etc.; and Rambam forbids and explains all the above when the hour requires it as Nekudot Yosef wrote in Sanhedrin there regarding Chananiah Mishael and Azariah ; otherwise no difficulty of public [even a cloak of fine wool, etc.]; and so Tosafot in Ketubot 33b; but nevertheless it is not settled for there for his benefit; and Daniel who gave himself for prayer in his house; and Rosh brought proof there in Avodah Zarah from Yerushalmi ; R. Abba bar Zavina was a tailor with a gentile who said eat nevelah or I kill you; he said if you wish to kill ; kill for I will not eat; and presumably in private in the gentile's house; but Rashi wrote specifically when the gentile intends to make him transgress religion; and so is that Yerushalmi case and Daniel's case; but Chananiah Mishael and Azariah do not imply so as stated; and from Tosafot implies like Rashi's view who wrote in Avodah Zarah all this 27b s.v. yachol. And if he wishes to be stringent, etc. like R. Abba, etc.; and in Sanhedrin 74b s.v. ktol he wrote that incident, etc. ; because it was for his benefit as Tosafot wrote there and Ramban chapter 4 of Shabbat.

segments.he: ואם יוכל כו'. דאפילו שבות דשבת אסור בהפסד ממון כמ"ש בפט"ז דשבת (קכ"א א') א"א כבה כו' ובפ"ב די"ט (כ"ב א') כי קמיבעיא לי משום הפסד ממון ובפ' בתרא דע"ז (ע' א') כמה כיסי משתכחי כו' ולא ידענא כו' וכיוצא בו הרבה:
segments.en: And if he can, etc. For even rabbinic Shabbat violation is forbidden with monetary loss as stated in end of chapter 19 of Shabbat (121a) it is impossible to extinguish, etc.; and in chapter 2 of Yom Tov (22a) for I am asked because of monetary loss; and in last chapter of Avodah Zarah (70a) how many purses are found, etc. and I do not know, etc.; and many similar.

segments.he: ובמקום כו'. כמ"ש בר"פ בתרא דקדושין (ע"א א') ישבו ובדקו כו' ופירשו ואפילו בממונו ממ"ש בסנהדרין ע"ג א' אי מהתם ה"א בנפשיה אבל כו' אלמא אי לאו קרא ה"א דאפילו להציל נפש חבירו אינו מחוייב להוציא ממונו אבל משמע שם מדבריו דאכל מל"ת אינו מחוייב להוציא ממונו דהוכיח מדכתבה תורה בכל מאדך בע"ז והוא שלא כדברי הר"ן הנ"ל:
segments.en: And in a place, etc. As stated in last chapter of Kiddushin (71a) they sat and examined, etc.; and they explained even with his money from what is stated in Sanhedrin 73a if from there you would say for himself ; but, etc.; evidently if not for a verse you would say even to save another's life he is not obligated to give his money; but it implies there from his words that for all negative commandments he is not obligated to give his money ; he proved from Torah writing "with all your might" regarding idolatry; and this is not like Ran cited above.

segments.he: דהיינו כו' מישראל. שם:
segments.en: That is, etc. , of Israel. There.

segments.he: אם העובד כוכבים כו'. גמ' שם והא אסתר כו':
segments.en: If the gentile intends, etc. Gemara there ; but Esther, etc.:

segments.he: (ליקוט) אם העובד כוכבים מכוין כו'. טור ולא כ' אלא גבי פרהסיא כתי' הגמ' שם אבל רש"י שם ד"ה שדי כו' כ' בפרהסיא וכן בגזירת המלכות (וכ"כ הרמב"ן בכתובות ג' ב' דלא כהראב"ד ע"ש) ובהג"א פ"א דכתובות ס"ד ד"ה ולקמן נסתפק בזה אבל רש"י ס"ל אף בג' עבירות להנאת עצמן שרי וע"ש בד"ה הני קוקי כו' (וע"ל ס"ק י"ב וס"ק י"ד) (ע"כ):
segments.en: (Extract) If the gentile intends, etc. Tur and the Gemara only wrote regarding public; but Rashi there s.v. shedei, etc. wrote in public; and so regarding royal decree (and so Ramban in Ketubot 3b unlike Ra'avad ; see there); and in Hagahot Ashri chapter 1 of Ketubot 64 s.v. velakman I was uncertain on this; but Rashi holds even for three prohibitions for their own benefit it is permitted ; see there s.v. hani kuki, etc. (and see s.k. 12 and 14) (end).

segments.he: אפי' על כו'. שם:
segments.en: Even upon, etc. There.

segments.he: על ישראל לבדם. מדפריך שם והא אסתר פרהסיא הוה ולא פריך דגזירת המלכות היתה:
segments.en: Upon Israel alone. From the fact that it challenges there "but Esther was in public" ; and does not challenge that it was a royal decree.

segments.he: ודוקא כו'. דהרי אלישע בעל כנפים נטלן מראשו והטעם דהרי יכולין להעבירו בע"כ שיטלוהו מראשו ויושיבוהו בבית האסורין וז"ש בסנהדרין שם קרקע עולם היא ור"ל שיכולין לכוף אותה בע"כ והקשה שם הר"ן היאך מסר עצמו אלישע בתחלה וכן דניאל בשביל התפלה וכן כל הנך שכ' לעיל במדרש ש"ט מה לך כו' ותי' דרשאי להחמיר על עצמו למסור במקום שא"צ כמש"ל וכ"כ נ"י בסנהדרין שם על מש"ש דקרקע עולם כו' כנ"ל וכתב דאסור למסור עצמו במקום שא"צ והא דאלישע בעל כנפים וכן חנניה מישאל ועזריה ומדרש ש"ט הנ"ל היינו מפני שהיתה השעה צריכה לכך וכ"כ בד"מ משמו וז"ש כאן מיהו אם כו' וצ"ע שהרי בש"ע פסק שלא כדברי נ"י כמש"ל ואם ירצה כו' ולא הגיה שם כלום ודא ודא אחת היא:
segments.en: And specifically, etc. For Elisha ba'al kenafayim took them from his head; and the reason ; they can force him to remove them from his head and seat him in prison; and this is what is stated in Sanhedrin there ; the world is ground (meaning they can force it against his will); and Ran challenged there how did Elisha initially give himself up; and likewise Daniel for prayer; and likewise all those cited above in midrash Shochar Tov ; what do you, etc.; and they explain one may be stringent on himself to give up life where not necessary as stated; and so Nekudot Yosef in Sanhedrin there on what is stated the world is ground, etc. as stated; and he wrote forbidden to give oneself up where not necessary; and that Elisha ba'al kenafayim and Chananiah Mishael and Azariah and midrash Shochar Tov cited ; because the hour required it; and so Darkei Moshe in his name; and this is what he wrote here however if, etc.; and requires study for behold in Shulchan Aruch he ruled not like Nekudot Yosef as stated; and if he wishes, etc. and he emended nothing there ; certainly one matter.

segments.he: אפילו כו' ושלא כו'. גמ' שם:
segments.en: Even so, and not so. Gemara there.

segments.he: ואפילו אין העובד כוכבים כו'. דהא אפילו להתרפאות משלשה דברים אלו אסור ואמרינן בסנהדרין שם (ע"ה א') מעשה כו' בשלמא אשת איש כו' ואע"ג דמשום הנאתו ובפ' בתרא דיומא (פ"ב א') עוברה שהריחה כו' שאין לך דבר כו'. ר"ן בפ' כ"ש ע"ש (שכתב וקשה קצת כו' ואלו הקושיות כו'):
segments.en: And even if the gentile, etc. For it is forbidden even to obtain healing through any of these three transgressions. Sanhedrin 75a relates the incident, etc.; the Gemara explains that this is understandable in the case of a married woman, etc., even though the coercer's purpose was his own gratification. Likewise, at the end of Yoma, regarding a pregnant woman who smelled food, etc., it states that nothing stands before danger to life, etc. See the Ran in the chapter Kol Sha'ah, who writes that this is somewhat difficult, etc., and discusses these questions, etc.

segments.he: ודוקא כו'. תוס' דיבמות נ"ג ב' ד"ה אין אונס כו' ובכתובות ג' ב' ד"ה ולידרוש כו' ובסנהדרין שם ע"ד ב' ד"ה והא כו' וש"מ:
segments.en: Specifically, etc. Tosafot to Yevamos 53b, s.v. “There is no coercion,” etc.; Kesubos 3b, s.v. “Let them expound,” etc.; and Sanhedrin 74b, s.v. “But Esther,” etc. This proves the ruling.

segments.he: וכל איסור עבודת כוכבים כו'. דהא אשירה דאין מתרפאין מהן אינו אלא לאו בעלמא לא ידבק כו' כמ"ש בפ"ג דפסחים (מ"ח א') וסוף מכות וש"מ וכן ההוא מעשה דסנהדרין הנ"ל לא היתה אלא לאו דלא תקרבו וי"א דרק מדרבנן וכנ"ל (ע"ל סי' ק"נ ס"ק ד' וסי' קנ"ה ס"ק ט"ז י"ז כ"ב) אלא דקשה הא דאמרינן בסנהדרין שם דאלת"ה הני קוואקי כו' אלמא דל"ק אלא משום דפרהסיא הוא ואסור אף בשאר מצות דמשום עבודת כוכבים לא משני מידי דשם אף בהנאת עצמן אסור כנ"ל תי' הר"ן ונ"י שם דשם כיון שהוא משום לפני עור כו' אינו בכלל עבודת כוכבים וז"ש אבל אלאו כו':
segments.en: And every idolatry prohibition, etc. For the asheirah from which one is not healed is only a plain negative commandment lo yidbak, etc. as stated in chapter 3 of Pesachim (48a) and end of Makot ; learn from this; and likewise that incident in Sanhedrin cited was only negative commandment of lo tikravu; and some say only rabbinically as stated (see siman 150 s.k. 4 and siman 155 s.k. 16, 17, 22); except it is difficult that we say in Sanhedrin there ; if so these kuki, etc.; evidently no difficulty except because it is public and forbidden even for other mitzvot because of idolatry makes no difference ; there even for their own benefit forbidden as stated; Ran and Nekudot Yosef explained there since it is because of lifnei iver, etc. it is not in the category of idolatry ; and this is what he wrote but a plain prohibition, etc.

segments.he: ועובד כוכבים כו'. כ"כ ר"ת בתוס' דסנהדרין הנ"ל ובכתובות בד"ה הנ"ל דפריך ולידרוש כו' ובסנהדרין שם דפריך והא אסתר כו' ולא פריך גילוי עריות הוי וגם התי' לא היה עולה הנאת עצמן כנ"ל וכ"כ הרמב"ן ועבר"ן פ' כ"ש ובפ' בתרא דיומא אבל תוס' תי' משום דקרקע עולם היתה כנ"ל ופליגי אר"ת וכן ש"פ:
segments.en: And a gentile, etc.

segments.he: עובדי כוכבים כו'. ירושלמי פ"ח דתרומות והביאו הר"ש שם מתני' י"ב וכר' יוחנן והרמב"ם פסק כר"ל משום ההוא עובדא דריב"ל שם וצ"ע:
segments.en: So Rabbeinu Tam in Tosafot of Sanhedrin cited and in Ketubot s.v. cited who challenges and to expound, etc.; and in Sanhedrin there who challenges but Esther, etc. and does not challenge gilui arayot; and also the explanation was not for their own benefit as stated; and so Ramban and Ramban chapter 21 and last chapter of Yoma; but Tosafot explain because the world was ground as stated; and they disagree with Rabbeinu Tam; and so Shach.

segments.he: וכן כו'. מתני' שם:
segments.en: And likewise, etc. Mishnah there.

segments.he: כ"מ כו'. סנהדרין ס"א וכרבא:
segments.en: As is stated kill, etc. and exempt.

segments.he: (ליקוט) כ"מ שנא' יהרג כו' ופטור. כרבא בסנהדרין דאמר פטור וכתי' ראשון בתוס' שם אבל הרא"מ פי' כתי' השני שלא נעשה מעולם לשם עבודת כוכבים אלא מאהבת ויראת אדם כגון אנדרטי והמן דלתי' הראשון קשה דתנן הפוער כו' אע"ג דמתכוין לבזוייה והזורק כו' אע"ג דמתכוין למרגמיה. הג"מ פ"ג ס"ק ב' ע"ש והריב"ש תירץ הקושיא והביאו כ"מ ע"ש (ע"כ):
segments.en: Like Rava in Sanhedrin who said exempt; and the first version in Tosafot there; but Ra'avan explained the second version that it was never for idolatry but from love and fear of man such as monuments and Haman whose first door is difficult for our mishnah one who exposes, etc. even though he intends to disgrace; Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 3 s.k. 2 ; see there; and Rivash resolved the difficulty and Knesset HaGedolah brought it ; see there (end).

segments.he: ודוקא שלא יוכל לברוח כו'. ואף שתחלתן באונס כמ"ש בספ"ד דכתובות (נ"א ב') הני נשי דגנבי כו' ודאי שבקינהו כו'. הריב"ש (ע"כ):
segments.en: Specifically where he cannot escape, etc. This applies even though the matter began under coercion, as stated at the end of the fourth chapter of Kesubos 51b regarding women who were abducted, etc.: certainly, if their captors released them, etc. Rivash.

en_segments: Except, etc. There in Sanhedrin; and although R. Yishmael disagrees we rule like R. Yochanan who said they counted and concluded; and so the sugya in chapter 2 of Pesachim and chapter 2 of Ketubot (19a) and the last chapter of Yoma ; learn from this.
If he is in private, etc. Gemara there.

And if he wishes, etc. As stated in end of chapter 19 of Shabbat ; every mitzvah they handed over, etc.; and Elisha ba'al kenafayim in chapter 4 (end) of Shabbat; and R. Akiva and R. Yehudah ben Bava and all martyrs of the kingdom who gave themselves for private mitzvot; and we say in Shochar Tov ; what are these wounds between your hands; and he said those who struck me in my lovers' house ; these wounds caused me to love my Father in heaven; why do you go out to be stoned for keeping Shabbat, to be burned for eating matzah, to be killed for circumcising my son, etc.; and in Pesachim 53b ; what did they see, etc.; and Tosafot there s.v. mah. And from Rabbenu Chananel ; image, etc.; and Rambam forbids and explains all the above when the hour requires it as Nekudot Yosef wrote in Sanhedrin there regarding Chananiah Mishael and Azariah ; otherwise no difficulty of public [even a cloak of fine wool, etc.]; and so Tosafot in Ketubot 33b; but nevertheless it is not settled for there for his benefit; and Daniel who gave himself for prayer in his house; and Rosh brought proof there in Avodah Zarah from Yerushalmi ; R. Abba bar Zavina was a tailor with a gentile who said eat nevelah or I kill you; he said if you wish to kill ; kill for I will not eat; and presumably in private in the gentile's house; but Rashi wrote specifically when the gentile intends to make him transgress religion; and so is that Yerushalmi case and Daniel's case; but Chananiah Mishael and Azariah do not imply so as stated; and from Tosafot implies like Rashi's view who wrote in Avodah Zarah all this 27b s.v. yachol. And if he wishes to be stringent, etc. like R. Abba, etc.; and in Sanhedrin 74b s.v. ktol he wrote that incident, etc. ; because it was for his benefit as Tosafot wrote there and Ramban chapter 4 of Shabbat.

And if he can, etc. For even rabbinic Shabbat violation is forbidden with monetary loss as stated in end of chapter 19 of Shabbat (121a) it is impossible to extinguish, etc.; and in chapter 2 of Yom Tov (22a) for I am asked because of monetary loss; and in last chapter of Avodah Zarah (70a) how many purses are found, etc. and I do not know, etc.; and many similar.

And in a place, etc. As stated in last chapter of Kiddushin (71a) they sat and examined, etc.; and they explained even with his money from what is stated in Sanhedrin 73a if from there you would say for himself ; but, etc.; evidently if not for a verse you would say even to save another's life he is not obligated to give his money; but it implies there from his words that for all negative commandments he is not obligated to give his money ; he proved from Torah writing "with all your might" regarding idolatry; and this is not like Ran cited above.
That is, etc. , of Israel. There.
If the gentile intends, etc. Gemara there ; but Esther, etc.:

(Extract) If the gentile intends, etc. Tur and the Gemara only wrote regarding public; but Rashi there s.v. shedei, etc. wrote in public; and so regarding royal decree (and so Ramban in Ketubot 3b unlike Ra'avad ; see there); and in Hagahot Ashri chapter 1 of Ketubot 64 s.v. velakman I was uncertain on this; but Rashi holds even for three prohibitions for their own benefit it is permitted ; see there s.v. hani kuki, etc. (and see s.k. 12 and 14) (end).
Even upon, etc. There.
Upon Israel alone. From the fact that it challenges there "but Esther was in public" ; and does not challenge that it was a royal decree.

And specifically, etc. For Elisha ba'al kenafayim took them from his head; and the reason ; they can force him to remove them from his head and seat him in prison; and this is what is stated in Sanhedrin there ; the world is ground (meaning they can force it against his will); and Ran challenged there how did Elisha initially give himself up; and likewise Daniel for prayer; and likewise all those cited above in midrash Shochar Tov ; what do you, etc.; and they explain one may be stringent on himself to give up life where not necessary as stated; and so Nekudot Yosef in Sanhedrin there on what is stated the world is ground, etc. as stated; and he wrote forbidden to give oneself up where not necessary; and that Elisha ba'al kenafayim and Chananiah Mishael and Azariah and midrash Shochar Tov cited ; because the hour required it; and so Darkei Moshe in his name; and this is what he wrote here however if, etc.; and requires study for behold in Shulchan Aruch he ruled not like Nekudot Yosef as stated; and if he wishes, etc. and he emended nothing there ; certainly one matter.
Even so, and not so. Gemara there.

And even if the gentile, etc. For it is forbidden even to obtain healing through any of these three transgressions. Sanhedrin 75a relates the incident, etc.; the Gemara explains that this is understandable in the case of a married woman, etc., even though the coercer's purpose was his own gratification. Likewise, at the end of Yoma, regarding a pregnant woman who smelled food, etc., it states that nothing stands before danger to life, etc. See the Ran in the chapter Kol Sha'ah, who writes that this is somewhat difficult, etc., and discusses these questions, etc.
Specifically, etc. Tosafot to Yevamos 53b, s.v. “There is no coercion,” etc.; Kesubos 3b, s.v. “Let them expound,” etc.; and Sanhedrin 74b, s.v. “But Esther,” etc. This proves the ruling.

And every idolatry prohibition, etc. For the asheirah from which one is not healed is only a plain negative commandment lo yidbak, etc. as stated in chapter 3 of Pesachim (48a) and end of Makot ; learn from this; and likewise that incident in Sanhedrin cited was only negative commandment of lo tikravu; and some say only rabbinically as stated (see siman 150 s.k. 4 and siman 155 s.k. 16, 17, 22); except it is difficult that we say in Sanhedrin there ; if so these kuki, etc.; evidently no difficulty except because it is public and forbidden even for other mitzvot because of idolatry makes no difference ; there even for their own benefit forbidden as stated; Ran and Nekudot Yosef explained there since it is because of lifnei iver, etc. it is not in the category of idolatry ; and this is what he wrote but a plain prohibition, etc.
And a gentile, etc.

So Rabbeinu Tam in Tosafot of Sanhedrin cited and in Ketubot s.v. cited who challenges and to expound, etc.; and in Sanhedrin there who challenges but Esther, etc. and does not challenge gilui arayot; and also the explanation was not for their own benefit as stated; and so Ramban and Ramban chapter 21 and last chapter of Yoma; but Tosafot explain because the world was ground as stated; and they disagree with Rabbeinu Tam; and so Shach.
And likewise, etc. Mishnah there.
As is stated kill, etc. and exempt.

Like Rava in Sanhedrin who said exempt; and the first version in Tosafot there; but Ra'avan explained the second version that it was never for idolatry but from love and fear of man such as monuments and Haman whose first door is difficult for our mishnah one who exposes, etc. even though he intends to disgrace; Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 3 s.k. 2 ; see there; and Rivash resolved the difficulty and Knesset HaGedolah brought it ; see there (end).

Specifically where he cannot escape, etc. This applies even though the matter began under coercion, as stated at the end of the fourth chapter of Kesubos 51b regarding women who were abducted, etc.: certainly, if their captors released them, etc. Rivash.
